semantic_correction.stem: Bedside RNs report burnout associated with short staffing, unpredictable schedules and excessive administrative work. A unit quality-improvement team asks for staff proposals. Which proposal by an RN best reflects NIOSH's systems approach to healthcare-worker wellbeing?

options.A: Recommend expanding resilience and mindfulness resources while leaving staffing, schedules, workload, and administrative processes unchanged.
options.B: Ask each nurse to create an individual coping plan and review adherence before the team considers changes to working conditions or unit operations.
options.C: Bring staff-identified work-system drivers to the QI team and advocate for operational changes while using individual wellbeing resources as support.
options.D: Increase mandatory overtime to stabilize staffing coverage first, then evaluate burnout after the schedule has been sustained for several months.

semantic_correction.rationale: NIOSH's Impact Wellbeing campaign identifies systemic factors such as inadequate staffing, demanding work schedules and excessive administrative work as root contributors to healthcare-worker burnout. The Impact Wellbeing Guide explicitly uses a systems approach: go beyond encouraging self-care and individual resilience and focus on operational-level improvements, while building trust through two-way communication and staff involvement. NIOSH also provides guidance specifically for healthcare workers to advocate for use of the Guide and for reducing process and operational burdens that contribute to burnout. Option C appropriately places the bedside RN in a participation/advocacy role: bring staff-identified system drivers into QI and advocate for operational improvement, with individual wellbeing resources as supportive rather than primary treatment of the system problem. A and B make individual resilience/coping the principal intervention while leaving work conditions unchanged. D worsens a recognized work-schedule burden. Therefore C is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Participate in workplace quality improvement by identifying modifiable system drivers of healthcare-worker burnout and advocating for operational improvements rather than relying primarily on individual resilience interventions.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired the nurse-manager decision-making frame, rebuilt the item around a bedside RN's participation and advocacy within QI, normalized difficulty from hard to medium, and removed the conspicuous correct-answer length cue.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original stem assigned the candidate a nurse-manager role even though the NIOSH Guide is designed primarily for leaders. The revision uses NIOSH's separate healthcare-worker advocacy guidance and limits the RN to identifying system drivers and contributing to QI/advocacy rather than exercising executive authority.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0220 tests systems-based analysis of repeated medication errors and process redesign. V2-Q0223 tests use of research/guidelines for an evidence-informed practice recommendation. V2-Q0272 tests recognition of occupational work-system drivers and bedside-RN advocacy/QI participation around professional wellbeing.

option_audit.A: Plausible because resilience and mindfulness resources can support workers, but NIOSH explicitly advises going beyond individual resilience to address operational drivers.
option_audit.B: Plausible because individual coping matters, but making coping adherence a prerequisite to reviewing working conditions wrongly shifts responsibility away from the identified system factors.
option_audit.C: Correct. It keeps the RN within an entry-level participation/advocacy role while applying NIOSH's systems approach and staff-involvement principle.
option_audit.D: Plausible as a short-term staffing response, but unpredictable/demanding schedules and excessive workload are themselves identified burnout drivers; increasing mandatory overtime conflicts with the systems approach.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. C alone addresses the stated system drivers through QI participation and advocacy without giving the bedside RN managerial authority. A and B rely primarily on individual-level remedies; D intensifies a recognized work-system stressor.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four options are nearly equal in length and use parallel proposal language; the correct answer is not conspicuously longer.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: The revised item asks the newly licensed RN to participate in QI, identify staff-reported system factors and advocate through team processes, rather than manage staffing policy independently.
